title: Expected match count
prompt: Write expected_wins(n,p). Example: 20 games at .6 gives 12.
tests:
assert expected_wins(20,.6)==12, 'Expected wins are n times p'
assert expected_wins(0,.7)==0, 'Zero trials have zero expected wins'
assert expected_wins(10,1)==10, 'Certain wins give n'

title: Seeded outcomes
prompt: Write simulate(n,p,seed) using random.Random(seed) and one random() call per trial. Return a list of 0/1 outcomes. Example: p=1 returns n ones.
starter:
import random
def simulate(n,p,seed):
    # TODO: create one generator before the loop
    return []
solution:
import random
def simulate(n,p,seed):
    rng=random.Random(seed)
    return [int(rng.random()<p) for _ in range(n)]
tests:
a=simulate(20,.6,7)
r=random.Random(7)
assert a==[int(r.random()<.6) for _ in range(20)], 'Use one seeded stream and one draw per trial'
assert simulate(3,1,2)==[1,1,1] and simulate(3,0,2)==[0,0,0], 'Respect probability boundaries'
assert simulate(0,.5,2)==[], 'Zero trials give an empty list'
hint: Do not reseed inside the loop.

title: Expected toy reward
prompt: Write expected_reward(p,win_reward,loss_reward). Example: p=.5, win=2, loss=-1 gives .5.
tests:
assert expected_reward(.5,2,-1)==.5, 'Weight both rewards by their probabilities'
assert expected_reward(0,3,-2)==-2, 'At p=0 only loss reward remains'
assert expected_reward(1,3,-2)==3, 'At p=1 only win reward remains'
hint: A loss reward may already be negative.

title: Many simulated batches
prompt: Write batches(n,p,count,seed) using np.random.default_rng(seed).binomial and returning count sampled win counts. Example: n=0 yields all zeros.
tests:
a=batches(10,.4,20,8)
assert np.array_equal(a,np.random.default_rng(8).binomial(10,.4,size=20)), 'Use the specified seeded binomial generator'
assert a.shape==(20,) and ((a>=0)&(a<=10)).all(), 'Each batch count must lie between 0 and n'
assert np.array_equal(batches(0,.5,3,8),[0,0,0]), 'No trials means zero wins'
